overall_reason: The system UI stack (Segoe UI drew every glyph at 1440 per fonts.json; system-ui computed at 375) sets every role, which fits a product-UI (Operate) composition with the same ladder as a tuned library window, but a transform scales the whole window down, so the 22px head draws about 18px tall and every 10 to 11px label draws in a 9 to 11px box.

score.reason: T-LADDER: the declared sizes are fine, but the scale transform shrinks every role, and the sweep's text_floor hit records the result (a 9px glyph box for 11px type).

findings.title: Never shrink text to fit or to hide a content problem
findings.evidence: In dom-1440.json the h3 'Launch package' is set at 22px with a 29px line-height but draws 18px tall. 'Everything your team needs to publish.' (11px, 17px line) draws 11px tall, and 'Campaign launch' (10px, 16px line) draws 10px tall. That is a scale of about 0.62. On P43/01-evidence/tiles/1440-00.png and P43/01-evidence/tiles/375-00.png the nav, meta and button text are hard to read. The sweep's text_floor hit records 'a 9px glyph box for 11px type, a transform'.
findings.before: Window scaled to about 0.62 so it fits beside the thumbnail grid
findings.after: Render the window at 1:1 and give it the width it needs; crop or drop the thumbnail grid instead of scaling the type
findings.why: A transform shrinks the whole ladder at once, so the 10 and 11px labels draw at roughly 6 to 7px.

strengths: The underlying ladder is clear: 22/550 head, 13/600 window title, 12/500 card title, 10 to 11px labels.
